transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Yeah, nice to meet you too. Um, mostly I’m here because I’m just so tired. But it's... it's a weird kind of tired, you know? Like, sleep doesn’t even fix it. I can sleep and sleep, and then I try to do something simple, like unload the dishwasher, and it just feels like climbing a mountain. I have this set of plates, actually, they're these really heavy ceramic ones I got at a thrift store. I love them, they have this beautiful blue glaze, but lately just lifting them into the cupboard is exhausting. And I'm supposed to be reading for this certificate class I'm taking—I dropped out of college a while ago, so I'm trying to get this certificate to maybe get a better job—but even looking at the textbook is just... too much. My cat, Barnaby, he always sits right on the book when I try to read anyway. He's an orange tabby, very demanding. But yeah, the tiredness is just... it's a lot.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

I mean, I don't know if I'd call it depressed. I don't really feel sad, just... flat, I guess? Or maybe I just haven't really thought about my mood much because I was trying to reorganize my living room to make more space. I started sorting all my books by color the other day instead of reading them. Have you ever tried that? It looks so cool on the shelf, especially all the blue and green spines grouped together. I have a ton of these old vintage sci-fi paperbacks with those really weird, surreal covers. My dad gave them to me a few years ago when I moved out of my last apartment. He lives out in Ohio now, which is just... so flat. I drove out to see him last summer and it was literally just cornfields for hours and hours. I had to pull over at this bizarre little diner on the highway that sold ostrich burgers, of all things. I didn't try one, but they had a giant plastic ostrich outside. But um, wait, what did you ask me? Oh, feeling down. No, I don't think I'm sad or crying or anything like that. Just that heavy tired feeling I mentioned.
Do you find yourself getting very sleepy during the day?

Sleepy during the day? Um, I don't really think so. Not like nodding off or needing a nap or anything. I actually really hate taking naps because whenever I wake up, the light in the room is always that weird, harsh afternoon color, you know? It just makes me feel completely disoriented. Plus, if I try to lie down on the couch during the day, Barnaby just walks all over my chest. He doesn't have front claws—he was already like that when I adopted him from the shelter, which is a relief because I think declawing is actually really cruel, it's basically like cutting off their knuckles. 

But the shelter I got him from was in this amazing old brick building downtown that used to be a fire station. You can still see the outline in the brick where the huge garage doors used to be for the fire trucks. I always wondered if they kept the brass pole inside when they converted it. I think they don't even let firefighters use those poles anymore because someone could twist an ankle or something. My cousin twisted his ankle playing intramural softball last spring and had to wear this giant gray walking boot for like a month and a half. He complained about it constantly. But um, wait. Did you ask about my sleep?
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things?

Worrying? Um, no, I don't really think so. I wouldn't say I'm a nervous person or anything. I mean, I guess sometimes I wonder if I left the stove on when I leave the apartment, but my stove is this really old electric one with those coils that turn bright red. I actually ruined a really nice tea towel on one of those coils a few months ago. It was this beautiful linen one with little lemons printed all over it that I bought at a farmer's market. I love farmer's markets, but the one near my place only runs on Tuesdays, which is such a weird day for a market, right? Like, who is buying fresh radishes at 10 AM on a Tuesday? Mostly just retired people, I guess. There's this one older guy who always plays the accordion near the sourdough bread stand. He's actually really good, but he only ever plays sea shanties and he wears this little sailor hat. It's kind of loud, honestly, especially if you're just trying to buy some tomatoes. But um... wait, what did you ask me? Was it about the stove?
Have you felt low on energy like this for most of the time over the past two years?

Two years? Oh, wow, no. Definitely not that long. It's been maybe... I don't know, about three months of this really quiet, heavy feeling where I just don't want to do anything. Three months is actually exactly how long my sister stayed with me when she was between apartments. She brought all her houseplants with her, which was completely overwhelming. She has this one Monstera plant that is just massive, it practically took up half my dining room. I had to water it with a literal pitcher every three days. She was super particular about the water temperature, too—it had to be room temperature, not straight from the tap, because apparently cold water shocks the roots. I tried to keep a Brita pitcher on the counter just for the plants, but then I kept accidentally drinking it and it tasted like dirt. I don't know why, maybe I just imagined the dirt taste because I knew it was the plant water. I actually hate tap water anyway, I usually just buy those big gallon jugs from the grocery store. The plastic handles on those always dig into your fingers when you carry them up the stairs, though. I live on the third floor and the stairs are incredibly steep. But um... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, the energy thing. Yeah, just the last three months or so.
Have you been enjoying things less than you usually do?

Enjoying things less? Yeah, I guess so. I just... I stopped caring about the things that usually make me feel like myself. Like, I used to love sketching and going to gallery openings. There was this one gallery downtown that always served the best little cheese cubes and these tiny crackers with figs on them. I don't even really like figs, but on those crackers, they were amazing. They were right next to this bakery that made sourdough bread, and the smell would just drift over while you were looking at the art. The bakery had this huge neon sign shaped like a pretzel, which is weird because they didn't even sell pretzels, just bread and these really dry scones. I bought a blueberry scone there once and it was so crumbly it basically disintegrated in my car. I had blueberry crumbs in the passenger seat for like a month, and I couldn't vacuum it out because the hose at the car wash was broken. The guy working there just put a piece of masking tape over the coin slot, but it was peeling off, so people kept losing their quarters. Quarters are so annoying to carry around anyway, they make your wallet super heavy. 

But um... what was I saying? Oh, right. Yeah, I stopped doing all that stuff. Even cooking, yoga, playing tennis with my friend... I just don't care about any of it right now.
Before this started three months ago, have you ever had another period like this?

Another period like this? Um, let me think... no, I don't think I've ever felt quite like this before. It's weird because I usually have so much energy, like, I'm always the one organizing things. I actually threw a surprise party for my friend Sarah last year, and I made everything from scratch. I even baked this huge three-tier cake, which was a terrible idea because I don't really know how to stack cakes. It ended up leaning to the side like the Leaning Tower of Pisa, and I had to prop it up with these little wooden dowels I bought at the craft store. The craft store is so dangerous for me, honestly. I go in there for one thing, like dowels, and I come out with fifty dollars' worth of glitter and these tiny glass beads that I never end up using. They just sit in these little plastic organizers in my closet. My closet is a disaster right now, by the way. I have all these winter coats taking up space, and I don't even wear half of them. There's this one puffy coat that makes me look like a marshmallow, but it's so warm I can't bring myself to donate it. I tried to drop it off at the thrift store once, but the line of cars to donate was out into the street, so I just went to get coffee instead. I get iced coffee even in the winter, which people think is crazy, but hot coffee just burns my tongue and then I can't taste anything for the rest of the day. 

But um... wait, what did you ask me? Did I have this before? Yeah, no, this is the first time I've felt this... heavy.
Before this started three months ago, have you ever had another period like this?

Wait, didn't you just ask me that? Or... wait, did you mean like, before the three months? I'm pretty sure I just said this is the first time. I've never felt this down before. Usually, I'm the one who's up and doing a million things. Like that party I mentioned. Sarah was so surprised, she actually dropped her purse when everyone yelled. Her purse was this really cute vintage leather bag she found at a flea market, but the clasp was broken, so all her lipsticks rolled out onto the floor. She has so many lipsticks, all in these really similar shades of pink. I don't know how she tells them apart. I only wear chapstick, honestly. The cherry kind that comes in the little blue tube. I buy them in bulk because I'm always losing them in the couch cushions or the washing machine. Washing chapstick is the worst, it leaves these weird grease stains on your clothes that never come out, even if you use that special stain remover spray. The spray smells like harsh chemicals anyway, it always gives me a headache if I use too much of it. 

But yeah, like I said... this is the first time I've felt like this. Never before.
